title: Front Door vs Application Gateway vs Load Balancer
description: Compare Azure's three main traffic managers to choose the right one for your application architecture.

data.text: Azure offers three primary traffic management services: Load Balancer, Application Gateway, and Front Door. Each operates at a different layer and serves different scenarios.

cards.title: Load Balancer
cards.description: Layer-4 TCP/UDP load balancer for VNet resources.

cards.title: Application Gateway
cards.description: Layer-7 HTTP load balancer with WAF for VNet resources.

cards.title: Front Door
cards.description: Global layer-7 load balancer and CDN at the edge.

data.title: Common Combination
data.text: Many architectures combine Front Door or Application Gateway with an internal Load Balancer. Front Door handles internet traffic, then passes requests to an internal Load Balancer for distribution across VMs inside a VNet.

data.title: Choose the Right Load Balancer
data.description: For each scenario, pick Load Balancer, Application Gateway, or Front Door and explain your choice.
steps: A gaming company needs low-latency UDP traffic distribution inside a VNet.
An e-commerce site in one region needs WAF and path-based routing.
A SaaS app serves users globally and needs instant failover between regions.
data.expectedOutcome: You can clearly explain why each scenario maps to a specific service.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Load Balancer is for raw TCP/UDP speed inside a VNet.
Application Gateway adds HTTP awareness and WAF regionally.
Front Door is the global choice with edge caching and anycast routing.
